title: People Config Panel: compact admin + service identity flows
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight proposal for a consolidated 'People Config' panel — a compact surface that blends org/team membership, admin assignments, service identities (service accounts + api keys), and a condensed audit micro-timeline. Goal is to reduce clicks for common admin tasks (create service identity, rotate key, invite with suggested role bundles) while keeping full detail pages reachable.

Design principles (working):
- Compactness: one top-level panel for quick actions and status, expandable for details
- Progressive disclosure: surface most likely actions first (invite, create service identity, rotate key), full policy editor behind an "advanced" toggle
- Safety-by-default: confirmation for destructive actions and clearer previews of effective permissions
- Observability: small inline audit micro-timeline (last 5 events) and direct link to full audit view

Audience & scenarios:
- Org admins who need to onboard engineers quickly and issue service identities for CI
- Platform engineers who create service accounts and attach key rotation policies
- Security reviewers scanning membership changes and recent key rotations

Low-fi wireframe descriptions (left-to-right card stack on wide screen):
1) Header strip: org name, active-team breadcrumb, quick-search (people/service identities)
2) Snapshot row: 3 compact cards side-by-side
   - People snapshot: counts (Owners, Admins, Editors, Viewers), CTA "Invite + suggested bundle"
   - Service identities snapshot: count, CTA "New service identity" with a 3-step mini-wizard (name, attach bundle, create key)
   - Keys & rotations: shows number of active keys, upcoming rotations, CTA "Rotate all keys" (danger modal)
3) Middle pane: list with toggle between People / Service Identities. Each row shows primary metadata + 2 small action buttons (edit, audit). Row affordances: clickable name -> detail flyout.
4) Right rail (expandable): micro-audit timeline (last 5 events) + quick-filters (by user, by event-type). A "jump to full audit" link opens the audit console.

Mini-wizard: New service identity (3 steps inline modal)
- Step 1: Name + optional description + attach environment tag (dev/staging/prod)
- Step 2: Suggest role bundle (preset combos derived from common infra patterns: CI-runner, Batch-inference, Metrics-ingest). Each bundle shows an estimated scope and token limit recommendation.
- Step 3: Key output: ephemeral secret shown once with copy button and optional KMS binding checkbox. Default TTL: 30d (editable).
Notes: adding ephemeral-first behavior reduces long-lived key sprawl; show clear guidance on rotating TTL to match committers' lifecycle.

Compact policy editor (advanced):
- Inline JSON preview + human summary above ("This bundle grants: read embeddings, write logs")
- Quick-snapshots: toggle to view Effective Permissions by selected resource (Console, Dedicated, Private).
- Inline link to policy simulator (opens advanced tool).

Audit micro-timeline behavior:
- Each event shows time, actor, brief action, and one-click revert where supported (eg. revoke API key).
- Events are grouped by logical pairings (invite accepted, role changed) to reduce noise.
- Hover reveals context: which route/model or resource was affected.

Edge cases:
- External collaborators vs SSO-provisioned users: display provisioning source icon and a small tooltip about manageability (SSO-managed roles are read-only in console).
- Cross-team service accounts: allow adding to multiple teams with clear tenancy badge.
- Large orgs: pagination + server-side search + ability to pin commonly used identities to top.

Backlog & grooming notes (rough prioritization):
- M1 (next sprint): People snapshot + invite flow with suggested bundles (2d design, 3d eng) - "high impact, low dev"
- M2: Service identity mini-wizard + ephemeral key output (5d eng, 2d design) - "must for onboarding"
- M3: Audit micro-timeline + quick revoke (4d eng, 1d design) - security priority
- M4: Compact policy editor + effective permission preview (6d eng, 3d design) - complexity: needs policy-sim infra
- Nice-to-have: cross-team pinning, bulk invite via CSV, role templating UX (post-launch)

Acceptance criteria (first pass):
- Invite flow creates user and assigns chosen bundle; admin can verify assignment on the People snapshot within 30s of creation.
- New service identity wizard returns a one-time key that can be copied; key stored in org secret store when user opts-in.
- Audit micro-timeline displays at least the last 5 events and the revoke action succeeds in 1 API call.
- SSO-provisioned users show read-only role controls and a link to identity provider mapping doc.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Preset bundles: Who curates the initial list? (proposal: product + solutions eng -> seed 5 bundles for common infra flows)
- Default key TTL: Should it be org-policy configurable or user-scoped? (security leaning to org-policy)
- UX for multi-tenant service identities: show tenancy matrix or separate resource pages?
- Should role bundles include cost/latency risk hints (eg. powers that enable high-cost models)? Tradeoff: more info vs clutter.

Signals to measure success (post-launch):
- Time-to-first-service-identity (target < 10 minutes from panel open)
- Number of long-lived keys (>90d) created per org (target: reduce by 40% via ephemeral defaults)
- Admin task completion rates (invite, rotate, revoke) and support tickets for onboarding issues

Prototype notes / where to find mockups:
- Figma file: figma.com/redwood/people-panel (WIP frames: compact-cards, wizard-stepper)
- Prototype link: figma:prototype/people-config-miniwiz

Next steps for grooming session (owner: Ava):
- Review with security and solutions-eng (Nov 5) to lock fresh bundles
- Create JIRA EPIC with subtasks for M1..M4 and include engineering estimates
- UX: create 3 high-fidelity screens (desktop: cards + wizard, mobile: stacked single-column)

Loose notes / brainstorm fragments (keep here for iteration):
- Inline "danger slider" for rotating all keys to prevent accidental mass revocations
- "Suggested expiration" overlay when creating keys based on linked repository activity
- Provide a "sandbox" toggle to mark identities as non-prod that automatically applies stricter TTL and auditing

Document history:

- 2025-11-10 added wizard steps and suggested bundles (Miguel)
- 2025-12-15 incorporated security feedback and made audit timeline actionable (Priya)
